title: Synthetic coldstart rerank manifest and sanitation protocol
content:
Purpose:
This doc specifies the design and hygiene checks for a synthetic reranking evaluation focused on coldstart and low-frequency query slices. The goal is to produce a pairwise preference dataset and matching utility scripts for NDCG calculations that stress long-tail inputs and format variations so that onboarding model regressions are detectable and actionable.

High-level approach (summary):
- Create a curated seed list of head queries from production traces (opt-out sanitized), then generate synthetic perturbations to produce coldstart variants that are not represented in training logs.
- Produce pairwise candidate pools per query with controlled noise levels (semantic near-misses, distractor passages, paraphrase transforms).
- Run a two-stage labeling pipeline: crowd pairwise judgments (binary preference) followed by adjudication on ambiguous/conflict pairs.
- Compute NDCG@k with multiple relevance proxies (binary > graded mapping) and report slice-level deltas.

Sampling and generation steps: 
1) Seed selection (headset): 3,000 unique canonical queries sampled from production query logs (one per user session). These are filtered for PII and legal-sensitive categories.
2) Coldstart synth rules: For each seed, generate 8 variants using the following transforms (applied stochastically):
   - lexical paraphrase (synonym swaps, 1-3 tokens)
   - punctuation and casing jitter
   - structural shuffle (reorder clauses)
   - template insertion (insert 1-2 domain words)
   - back-translation via en->fr->en for semantic drift
   - add cold-context tags (e.g., "old forum post", "obscure version")
3) Long-tail augmentation: Add 2,000 hand-curated low-volume queries from specialist domains (finance/tax/legal/new product names) to simulate edge traffic.
4) Candidate generation: For each query variant, generate 10 candidate responses by mixing the following sources: top-10 host model outputs, search-retrieved passages, and hard negatives sampled from unrelated domains. Ensure class balance across candidates (roughly equal split across types).

Pairwise labeling protocol: 
- Each pair consists of (candidate_A, candidate_B, query_variant). Workers choose which of the two is better for the query. Options: A, B, or No Preference (tie).
- Label redundancy: 5 independent judgments per pair.
- Qualification test: workers must pass a 15-question gold set at >= 80% to participate.
- Adjudication: Pairs with no majority (>=3 votes) go to senior annotators for adjudication and free-text reasoning.
- Label format: store as a triplet (query_id, better_candidate_id, label_type) where label_type in {A,B,TIE,ADJ_A,ADJ_B}.

Quality control checks (sanitation):
- Spam heuristics: detect labelers with >20% extremely fast responses (<= 2s) or low variance. Those workers' batches are flagged for review.
- Pair sanity filters: discard pairs where both candidates are near-duplicates (cosine sim > 0.95) prior to labeling to avoid redundant judgments.
- Semantic coverage: ensure at least 20% of pairs per slice contain a distractor from a different domain to test robustness.

NDCG calculation details: 
- Relevance mapping: we convert pairwise outcomes into graded relevance for each candidate as follows: majority preference -> relevance 3, adjudicated preference -> relevance 4, tie -> relevance 1, explicit negative (flagged content) -> relevance 0.
- Ranking score: compute NDCG@1, @3, @5 per query_variant and aggregate per slice. Use logarithmic discounting base 2.
- Bootstrapped confidence intervals: for slice-level deltas, bootstrap queries 1,000 times to get 95% CI for NDCG differences between models.
- Delta thresholds for gating: absolute NDCG@5 drop > 0.015 and lower CI > 0.01 triggers a regression alert.

Slice taxonomy (operational definitions):
- Coldstart-paraphrase: seed variants generated by back-translation or heavy lexical paraphrase.
- Product-name-edge: queries containing tokens identified in the last 12 months as new SKUs.
- Rare-intent: queries with < 50 occurrences in production during the last 90 days.
- Long-response: expected answer length > 250 tokens (derived from server-side reference distribution).
- Formatting-variance: queries with code, tables, or lists in the prompt.
- Multi-turn-implicit: single-shot queries that imply multiple steps (e.g., "compare X and Y and recommend").

Per-slice sample targets and power notes: 
- For primary coldstart-paraphrase slice: target 2,400 query_variants (approx 3k seeds x .8 that produce paraphrases). With 10 candidates and 5 labels per pair we expect ~120k pair judgments.
- Power estimate: to detect a 1.5% absolute NDCG@5 difference at 80% power, we need ~2,000 independent queries for the slice (bootstrap validated).

Adjudication and dispute resolution: 
- Dispute window: product teams have 7 days to request re-adjudication on flagged pairs after initial labels are published. Requests must include a rationale and the slice.
- Re-adjudication class: senior annotator + applied-ml reviewer double-check. Re-adjudicated labels are marked as ADJ_* and override majority where applicable.

Reporting and dashboards: 
- Output artifacts: CSV manifest (query_id, slice, variant_text), candidate table (candidate_id, type, source_model, text), pairwise labels CSV, adjudication log, ndcg_summary per slice per model.
- Dashboards: per-model NDCG heatmap, sample inspection view linking to raw pair labels and annotator comments, adoption recommendation (pass/fail/gated).

Sanitation scripts and reproducibility: 
- Scripts: provide python notebooks: 01_manifest_build.ipynb, 02_candidate_generation.ipynb, 03_label_ingest_and_qc.ipynb, 04_ndcg_and_bootstrap.ipynb.
- Deterministic seeds: all generation scripts must set RNG seed and log transforms for reproducibility.
- Change log: any change to generation rules must be accompanied by a small re-run on a 5% holdout and a short diff report.

Acceptance criteria for onboarding: 
- No slice shows an NDCG@5 regression beyond thresholds in the gating config.
- Annotator QC: inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's alpha) >= 0.62 on primary slice.
- Coverage: each model rollout must include the primary coldstart slice and at least two additional slices (product-name-edge, formatting-variance).

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Relevance mapping calibration: current mapping from pairwise majority->graded relevance is heuristic. Need small pilot to map pairwise signals to graded relevance more rigorously (psychometric scaling?).
- Worker compensation tradeoffs: cost vs redundancy (5 labels standard) — consider dynamic redundancy for high-ambiguity pairs.
- Slice priority ordering for limited labeling budgets.

Immediate next steps (owner: Aisha):
- Lock seed set by 2026-01-18 and share manifest to gs://redwood-evals/synthetic/seed-v1.csv.
- Kickoff pilot run for 300 queries (all transforms) by 2026-01-28 to test labeling flow and the NDCG mapping heuristic.
- Create GitHub PR for ingestion pipeline (linked above).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on pair redundancy to provide high-quality adjudication signals for NDCG. If budget constrained, we can move to adaptive labeling where clear-majority pairs stop at 3 labels.
- The synthetic transforms were chosen to emulate plausible user obfuscation/variant behavior rather than adversarial attacks — separate adversarial pipeline should be created if desired.

Appendix (quick checklist):
- [ ] Seed CSV exported and redacted
- [ ] Candidate generator unit tests
- [ ] Crowd qualification gold set created
- [ ] Adjudication queue skeleton in labeling UI
- [ ] Notebook for NDCG bootstrapping committed

End of document.
